newsitem.title: FRANCE: Giat signs Abu Dhabi steel plant offset contract.
newsitem.headline: Giat signs Abu Dhabi steel plant offset contract.

text.p: French state-owned arms maker Giat Industries said on Monday it had signed a partnership agreement to set up a steel production plant in Abu Dhabi, as part of an industrial offset scheme for its Leclerc battle tanks.

Giat said in a statement it had agreed with Stainless Steel International, East West International and Bin Bandooq Group to set up a local firm, Stainlees Steel LLC, to create the region's first steel cutting plant for flat stainless steel products.
The plant, to be located in Abu Dhabi, will supply Abu Dhabi and Mideast markets with semi-finished products. The project requires 118 million dirhams, or $32 million, of investment.

The plant will be sited in the industrial zone of Abu Dhabi and will handle between 10,000-11,000 tonnes of steel, representing nearly 25 percent of the annual market for semi-finished products in the Middle East.
Production will start in 1997 and the plant will employ around 40 skilled workers.
The project is part of Giat's offset programme to re-invest in the local economy, following Abu Dhabi's 1993 order worth $3.62 billion for Leclerc battle tanks.
Stainless Steel International is a holding company in the Terruzzi group. East West International and Bin Bandooq are local companies, a Giat spokeswoman said.
